questions.stem: In a queue of 47 candidates, a candidate is 15th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 15+4 = 19. Back rank = 47 − 19 + 1 = 29.

questions.stem: In a queue of 38 candidates, a candidate is 11th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 25. New front rank = 11+3 = 14. Back rank = 38 − 14 + 1 = 25.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 37 km east, turns left and walks 72 km, then turns left and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 78. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 30 km along the initial direction and 72 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(30² + 72²) = 78 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 106 km west, turns left and walks 165 km, then turns left and walks 18 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 187. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 88 km along the initial direction and 165 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(88² + 165²) = 187 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 38 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 8 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 30 km along the initial direction and 40 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: G is the only daughter of E. E is the father of G. A is the son of G. D is the sister of E. How is E related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. E is the father of G, and G is A’s mother. Thus E is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: C is the brother of H. H is the mother of F. E is the father of C and H. How is C related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of F’s mother H. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the mother of H. D is the son of H. A is the father of H. How is D related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. A is a parent of H, and D is H’s son. Hence D is A’s grandchild.

Conclusions: I. V < U   II. U < T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural banking access = ka to re
rural credit growth = ni to vo
banking credit savings = ni pa ka
access growth savings = vo pa re
rural banking savings = pa to ka
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: vo. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: rural = to, banking = ka, access = re, credit = ni, growth = vo, savings = pa.
